content:
incident-bot: Pager — P99 latency SLO breached for customer 'AtlasPay' on route /v1/streams (region: us-west-2). Alert: p99=4.8s (SLO 3s), p95=1.2s, streaming stall rate increased, ongoing since ~03:12 UTC. Severity: P2.

alice: I'm on it. seeing a big spike in tail latency across a handful of instances serving the single-tenant pool.

bob: Confirmed. Metrics: token throughput steady but per-request completion times are spiking. Looks correlated with high concurrent sessions from AtlasPay (they sent a batch of unusually long system prompts).

carmen: Paging on-call. @oncall-engr can you triage? Also tagging infra since we might be hitting KV cache thrash.

oncall-engr: I'm here. quick question — do we have evidence it's a model-side compute issue vs network/backpressure?

dinesh: Initial traces show requests sit waiting inside the runtime's kvcache lookup path then stall during streaming flush. Example tail trace: `runtime/serve.go:241 waitForKVCache -> compileAndDispatch -> streamFlush`

eva: I'm pulling per-instance flame graphs. Early signs of repeated cache evictions for long-prefix requests. AtlasPay's prompts include long instruction blocks + repeated context IDs, likely causing prefix churn.

alice: Customer impact check: AtlasPay reports intermittent 5–8s response delays for interactive chat. No data loss but UX severely degraded.

oncall-engr: ok. Immediate mitigations we can attempt: 1) temporary per-customer concurrency cap, 2) route AtlasPay to fallback stateless model variant (lower mem, faster kv lookups), 3) disable prefix prefetching on their route. Which should we try first?
bob: I suggest 1 then 2. Cap concurrency to their committed qps to reduce thrash. Also prepare a route change to `redwood-small-stateless-v1` as fallback.
carmen: I'll open a quick runbook item and add to incident timeline.

alice: Applying temporary quota now with `rbw admin set-quota --customer atlaspay --concurrency 12`

alice: Quota applied. Monitoring p99...

incident-bot: Action recorded: quota-change by alice at 03:21 UTC.

bob: Noticed immediate drop in queued requests on several GPUs, p99 fell from 4.8s -> 2.6s within 30s. Still above SLO but improved. Streaming stalls reduced but not eliminated.
dinesh: Preparing route switch. Will create new routing rule to prefer stateless fallback for atlaspay route. Command: `rbw route update --customer atlaspay --priority fallback --model redwood-small-stateless-v1`
eva: Heads-up: fallback has lower quality for some prompts but should reduce kv-dependent stalls. We should inform CS to warn AtlasPay about temporary quality delta.
carmen: Route change ready for canary. Rolling to 10% of AtlasPay traffic for 60s.
oncall-engr: Initiating canary.

incident-bot: Route update event: `route-update` canary started by dinesh at 03:26 UTC (10% traffic).

bob: Canary looks healthy. Those sessions see stable streaming and p99 ~1.4s. No streaming stalls observed in canary slice.
alice: Gradually increasing to 50% now. Watching client-side errors.
carmen: CS (not present) asked for a short customer note. Suggest: "We're seeing elevated latency caused by unusually long prompts and high concurrency. We've applied temporary safeguards and may route a subset of your traffic to a faster stateless model to restore responsiveness."
dinesh: Increasing to 100% fallback.

incident-bot: Route update event: `route-update` rolled to 100% at 03:33 UTC.
bob: After full rollback to stateless fallback, p99 stabilized to 1.1s, p95 0.9s, streaming stalls effectively gone. SLO appears met now.
eva: Confirming kvcache eviction rates dropped ~80% post-fallback. Flame graphs show no long-tail wait stacks.
oncall-engr: Great. Now root cause analysis notes: AtlasPay sent a set of long, repetitive system prompts with many unique prefixes causing excessive KV cache churn in the single-tenant pool. Under high concurrency this amplified tail latency.
alice: Next steps for remediation: 1) Work with model team to make kvcache eviction policy more shard-friendly for single-tenant workloads. 2) Add automatic conservative per-customer concurrency defaults when long-prefix patterns detected. 3) Improve monitoring alert to include kvcache eviction rate so we can page earlier.
carmen: I'll create tickets for the above and tag eng-runtime and eng-ml. Also draft customer comms.
eva: Also recommend we add a fast-path config to temporarily convert routes to stateless fallback automatically when kv eviction crosses threshold.

dinesh: Logging snippets for timeline (for postmortem):
```
03:12:42 UTC - incident-bot: p99 breach triggered (4.8s)
03:18:05 UTC - alice: applied customer concurrency cap
03:26:10 UTC - dinesh: started 10% canary -> redwood-small-stateless-v1
03:33:01 UTC - dinesh: rolled to 100% fallback
03:34:20 UTC - metrics: p99 -> 1.1s
03:37:00 UTC - incident closed to P2 monitoring
```
alice: Customer update sent by CS: "We've temporarily routed some traffic to a faster inference path to restore responsiveness. We're investigating and will follow up with details and timeline."
oncall-engr: Any data loss or model degradation reported by customer?
alice: AtlasPay noted slightly different phrasing from fallback model on a small subset. No functional failures.
carmen: Postmortem owners: eng-runtime (dinesh), eng-ml (eva), product (alice). I'll assign and set review in 72 hours.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (P2) at 03:37 UTC. All follow-ups logged.
bob: Still recommend we leave quota cap for 2 hours then gradually lift while monitoring.
alice: Agree. I'll set `rbw admin set-quota --customer atlaspay --concurrency 24 --expires 2026-03-15T06:00:00Z` to keep reduced cap.
carmen: Thanks all. Adding to incident channel for postmortem drafting. :thumbsup:
